stages.name: Growth vs environment
stages.title: Growth vs environment
stages.sub: Why pursuing economic growth can pull against protecting the environment.

steps.q: A country's factories pump out more smoke and use up more raw materials as they produce more. Left alone, will this pollution and resource use tend to fall by itself?
steps.right: No, it will tend to keep rising
steps.wrong: Yes, firms will cut it back on their own
steps.hint: Think about what pollution and resource depletion actually are: costs the firm does not have to pay for.

steps.q: A government wants factories to produce more cars, more steel and more energy this year, while also wanting less pollution and less resource use overall. Can both targets move in the direction the government wants at the same time?
steps.right: Not easily, they tend to pull apart
steps.hint: More output from factories usually brings more of the harms the other target wants to shrink.

steps.q: To force firms to pollute and deplete less while output is rising, the government makes them install filters and use costlier materials. Does this raise or lower the firms' costs of producing that extra output?
steps.wrong: It has no effect on their costs
steps.hint: Filters and cleaner materials are not free for the firm to add.

steps.q: If chasing higher output pushes pollution and depletion up, and cutting pollution and depletion pushes up firms' costs and slows output, can the government fully achieve growth and a protected environment together?
steps.right: No, achieving one tends to work against the other
steps.wrong: Yes, both can be fully achieved together
steps.hint: One objective wants more production, the other wants less harm from that production.
